SY425
Aging and the Life Course
0.5 Credit
Hours per week:
Lecture/Discussion: 3
This
course
explores various understandings and expressions of age, aging, and ageism in
contemporary society. It takes an intersectional approach to aging and old age across macro-structural, institutional, and micro-everyday realms. Themes to be discussed may include successful
aging; media representations; caregiving; interpersonal relations; dementia; consumerism and
consumption; and fitness and physical activity.
Additional Course Information
Prerequisites
Registration status: Year 4 Sociology program
Exclusions
SY452H
